name: Minnesota

statute.name: Minnesota Government Data Practices Act
statute.citation: Minn. Stat. ch. 13 (access § 13.03; opinions § 13.072; administrative complaint § 13.085)

response.rule_text: Requests must be complied with in an 'appropriate and prompt manner'; a denial must be communicated orally or in writing as soon as possible citing the specific legal basis, Minn. Stat. § 13.03, subd. 2(a), (f).

fees.labor_rule: No fee for searching when the requester only inspects; for copies, agency may charge actual costs of searching and retrieving including employee time, Minn. Stat. § 13.03, subd. 3(c).
fees.copy_rule: Actual costs of copying or electronic transmittal.
fees.waiver_rule: Fee waivers are not offered under the Act.

residency.rule_text: Any 'person' (individual, partnership, corporation, association, business trust) may request, Minn. Stat. § 13.03, subd. 3(a); § 13.02, subd. 10.

appeal.body: Commissioner of Administration (advisory opinion) or Office of Administrative Hearings; or district court
appeal.rule_text: An aggrieved person may ask the Commissioner of Administration for a non-binding opinion (Minn. Stat. § 13.072), file an OAH complaint within two years of the entity's initial failure to act (§ 13.085, subd. 2(b)), or sue in civil court (§ 13.08, subd. 4).

notes: deadline_days 730 = approximation of the 2-year OAH complaint limit. Commissioner opinions are not binding but court gives deference. Data Practices Act generally does not apply to the legislature. 'State agency' includes the University of Minnesota. Governor not extracted. Response has no day count for the general public.
